title: The customer page reads every representative row as designed
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have three active staff members at the test location with their "Sales Representative" switch on: sales rep A, sales rep B and sales rep C, so that each of the three fields holds a different name.
  • Use a customer with Service Labor set to sales rep A, Service Parts set to sales rep B and "Sales Representative - Part Sales" set to sales rep C, so the page shows all three representative rows.
  • Set the browser window to 1440 pixels wide with the zoom at 100%.
  • Open the design picture "customer-15-n2-page-three.png" (board 2.15) attached to this case beside the browser window at 100% (actual size). Names, numbers and dates in the pictures are sample data.
  • Open the customer's page in that browser window.
custom_steps: 1. Compare the representative rows with the picture of board 2.15.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • "Sales Representative - Service Labor", "Sales Representative - Service Parts" and "Sales Representative - Part Sales" show with their names as plain text.
  • They show in the window's order: Service Labor, then Service Parts, then Part Sales.
  • They are styled like the page's other rows, as in the picture.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11268 (Story 4, Give a customer default representatives)

  • S4-R19: “The customer page shows the representatives with the window's labels, in the window's order: "Sales Representative" or "Sales Representative - Service Labor", then "Sales Representative - Service Parts" when added, then "Sales Representative - Part Sales" when added. An empty one reads "Unassigned". The Sales Representative rows show on every customer, whether or not the customer has an address. The other fields on the page keep today's rule of showing only when the customer has an address.”
